title: Count Monobit Integers
summary: Given an integer n, count how many integers in the range from 0 to n have all bits in their binary representation the same.
statement: Given an integer n, count how many integers in the range from 0 to n have all bits in their binary representation the same.
constraints: Count integers from zero through n whose binary representation contains only one repeated bit value.
Zero qualifies with representation 0; positive qualifying values are 1, 3, 7, 15, and so on.
hints: Positive monobit representations cannot contain zero, so they are all-one masks.
Count masks no greater than n.
editorial: Count masks no greater than n.

tests.explanation: Both zero and one are monobit, so return two.
Zero plus one, three, and seven gives four values.
